Corollary
[Exponential kernel decay under holomorphy] Source: cheeger-gromov-taylor:page-0021, cheeger-gromov-taylor:page-0022 ↗ thm:c0-bounded-geometry-kernel-estimates 1. Corollary 3.2\group section-3

If $M$ has $C^0$-bounded geometry and $f(z)$ is holomorphic on (3.21) satisfying (3.22), then egin{equation} ag {3.23} |k_f(x_1,x_2)|\le Ce^{-Wr}, \end{equation}
Proof

\sketch The holomorphy hypothesis places $f$ in $\mathcal F_2^{\varphi ,A}$ with $\varphi (r)=Ce^{-Wr}$; apply the preceding theorem.

□

provided egin{equation} ag {3.24} ho (x_1,x_2)=r+2a. \end{equation}

Assume now that $M$ has $C^\infty $-bounded geometry. The bounded-curvature estimates control $k_f(x_1,x_2)$ for $ ho (x_1,x_2)\ge a$; near the diagonal we use the pseudodifferential representation below. Let $f(\lambda )\in S_{ ho ,0}^m(\mathbf R)$, i.e.,

egin{equation} ag {3.25} |f^{(j)}(\lambda )|\le C_j(1+|\lambda |)^{m-j ho }. \end{equation}

We use the standard symbol classes and pseudodifferential calculus; see \cite[Chapter~ II]{cgt-taylor-pdo}. From the representation

egin{equation} ag {3.26} f(\sqrt{-\Delta })u= rac{1}{2\pi }\int _{-\infty }^{\infty }\hat f(s)\cos s\sqrt{-\Delta }\, u\, ds, \end{equation}

use a partition of unity $1=\phi _1(s)+\phi _2(s)$, $\phi _1(s)\in C_0^\infty (-a,a)$, even, $\phi _1(s)=1$ for $|s|\le a/2$, to get

egin{align} f(\sqrt{-\Delta })u & = rac{1}{2\pi }\int _{-a}^{a}\phi _1(s)\hat f(s)\cos s\sqrt{-\Delta }\, u\, ds otag \ & \quad + rac{1}{2\pi }\int _{-\infty }^{\infty }\phi _2(s)\hat f(s)\cos s\sqrt{-\Delta }\, u\, ds otag \ & =F_1u+F_2u. ag {3.27} \end{align}

Note that

egin{equation} ag {3.28} F_2u=(1-\Delta )^{-k}\int _{-\infty }^{\infty } \left(1- rac{d^2}{ds^2} ight)^k(\phi _2(s)\hat f(s))\cos s\sqrt{-\Delta }\, u\, ds =(1-\Delta )^{-k}G_ku, \end{equation}

with $\| G_ku\| \le C_k\| u\| $. Thus the standard elliptic estimates and the Sobolev embedding theorem give

egin{equation} ag {3.29} \| F_2u\| _{C^l(B_a(x_1))}\le C_l\| u\| _{L^2}. \end{equation}

Furthermore, if $u$ is supported in $B_a(x_1)$,

egin{equation} ag {3.30} \| F_2u\| _{C^l(B_a(x_1))}\le C_{lk}\| u\| _{H^{-k}(B_a(x_1))}, \end{equation}

where the norm on the right is a Sobolev norm.

For the near-time term, egin{equation} ag {3.31} F_1u= rac{1}{2\pi }\int _{-a}^{a}\varphi _1(s)\hat f(s)\cos s\sqrt{-\Delta }\, u\, ds, \end{equation} with $u$ supported in $B_a(x_1)$. For $|s|\le a$, replace $\cos s\sqrt{-\Delta }$ by the standard geometrical-optics parametrix.

By shrinking $a$ if necessary, we can assume the parametrix for $\cos s\sqrt{-\Delta }$ is of the following form, in a normal coordinate system centered at $x_1$: egin{equation} ag {3.32} \cos s\sqrt{-\Delta }\, u(x)=\sum _{j=1}^{2}\int a_j(s,x,\xi )e^{i\varphi _j(s,x,\xi )}\hat u(\xi )\, d\xi . \end{equation} Here $\varphi _j$ solves the eikonal equation egin{equation} ag {3.33} rac{\partial }{\partial s}\varphi _j = (-1)^j\lambda _1^j(x,d\varphi _j)=(-1)^j(d\varphi _j,d\varphi _j)^{ rac12}, \end{equation} egin{equation} ag {3.34} \varphi _j(0,x,\xi )=x\cdot \xi \end{equation} for $|s|\le a$, $x\in B_{2a}(x_1)$; $a_j(s,x,\xi )$ is determined by the usual transport equations of geometrical optics (see for example, \cite[Chapter~ VIII]{cgt-taylor-pdo}), with $a_j(0,x,\xi )= rac12$. Now if $u$ is supported in $B_a(x_1)$, then, for $|s|\le a$, $\cos s\sqrt{-\Delta }\, u$ is supported in $B_{2a}(x_1)$. If we set $\hat g(s)=\varphi _2(s)\hat f(s)$, then $g(\lambda )\in S^{m}_{ ho ,0}$ differs from $f(\lambda )$ by an element of the Schwartz space $\mathcal S(\mathbb R)$ of rapidly decreasing functions. Thus we have egin{equation*} F_1u=\sum _{j=1}^{2}\int _{-a}^{a}\hat g(s)a_j(s,x,\xi )e^{i\varphi _j(s,x,\xi )}\hat u(\xi )\, d\xi \, ds+S_1u \end{equation*} egin{equation} ag {3.35} =\sum _j\int g(D_s)\! \left(a_j(s,x,\xi )e^{i\varphi _j(s,x,\xi )} ight)\Big|_{s=0}\hat u(\xi )\, d\xi +S_1u \end{equation} egin{equation*} =\int b(x,\xi )e^{ix\cdot \xi }\hat u(\xi )+S_1u, \end{equation*} where $S_1:\mathcal E'(B_a(x_1)) o C^\infty (B_{3a}(x_1))$, and $b(x,\xi )$ is given by the fundamental asymptotic expansion lemma for pseudodifferential operators. Thus egin{equation} ag {3.36} b(x,\xi )=\sum _{j=1}^{2}b_j(0,x,\xi ), \end{equation} where egin{equation} ag {3.37} b_j(s,x,\xi )=e^{-i\varphi _j(s,x,\xi )}g(D_s)\! \left(a_j(s,x,\xi )e^{i\varphi _j(s,x,\xi )} ight). \end{equation}

belongs to $S^m_{ ho ,1- ho }$ if $ ho \ge rac12$ with egin{equation} ag {3.38} b_j(s,x,\xi )\sim a_j(s,x,\xi )g\! \left( rac{\partial }{\partial s}\varphi _j ight)+\cdots . \end{equation} Hence using (3.33) and (3.34) we obtain egin{equation} ag {3.39} b(x,\xi )\sim g(\lambda _1(x,\xi ))+\cdots . \end{equation} The remainder terms in (3.38) and (3.39) sum to elements of $S^{m-(2 ho -1)}_{ ho ,1- ho }$ for $ ho \ge rac12$ and we have a complete asymptotic expansion for $ ho > rac12$.

Denoting by $\OPS ^m_{ ho ,\delta }$ the set of pseudodifferential operators with symbols in the class $S^m_{ ho ,\delta }$, we have the following conclusion.
